ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSAI-READY IMPLEMENTATION PRD
SECTION 01

Executive summary

The authoritative product and implementation brief for the team building Roomie. It defines the outcome, scope, requirements, release gates, and technical boundaries; it is not the product itself.

Trust is the product. Search is the entry point. A confident contact or viewing request is the first meaningful outcome.

What changed from the prior PRD

  • Positioned Roomie as the tentative renter/host product informed by BahayTrust's wider market, research, and trust thesis.
  • Reduced the primary audience to renters and hosts/property managers.
  • Made verified identity/listings, transparent costs, current photos, reviews, and explainable Roomie Scores the P0 trust layer.
  • Made occupancy, roommate context, lease terms, fees, and commute/neighborhood context required listing information.
  • Selected tenant MVP2's split map/list interaction as the usability baseline while retaining the strongest patterns from MVP1 and MVP3.
  • Moved live payments, escrow, ancillary services, AI valuation, investor analytics, and sales workflows behind the core rental journey.

Release definition

Now: validate

Verification, complete listings, map/list discovery, reviews, explainable score, messaging, viewing requests, and reporting.

Next: transact

Documents, contracts, payment tracking, receipts, and an optional regulated escrow pilot.

Later: expand

Ancillary services, roommate matching, deeper analytics, and institutional integrations.

Prototype status

The current MVPs are interactive React front-end prototypes with mock state and data. They validate interaction patterns; they do not yet prove production authentication, verification, moderation, payments, persistence, privacy controls, or marketplace operations.

Document rule. This web PRD is the current source of truth for implementation decisions. Prototype screens are evidence and interaction references, not production specifications when they conflict with this document.

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSVALIDATED BUILD DIRECTION
SECTION 02

What to build from the MVPs

The research is used here only to select a build direction. Detailed survey results remain in the source readout.

Outcome: Tenant MVP2 performed best. Use its split map/list discovery pattern as the deployable renter experience.
Keep

MVP2 map/list discovery, synchronized listing context, listing details, chat, and viewing requests.

Strengthen

Verified identity/listings, total costs, occupancy, current media, lease terms, location context, reporting, and stable navigation.

Defer

Payment processing, escrow, roommate matching, ancillary services, investor tools, and sales workflows.

Deployable v1 focus

  1. A renter can find an available listing, understand its complete cost and trust evidence, message the host, and request a viewing.
  2. A host can create and verify a listing, publish it, respond to inquiries, and manage viewing status.
  3. An operator can review verification evidence, moderate listings/users, resolve reports, and inspect an audit trail.
Build rule. Do not reproduce all three prototypes. Consolidate them into one production renter flow based on MVP2 and one production host flow based on the strongest host screens.

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSPRODUCT DEFINITION
SECTION 03

Product definition

Who Roomie serves, what problem it solves, and where the next MVP stops.

Problem statement

Metro Manila renters often search through fragmented, inconsistently structured listings where host identity, price, occupancy, photos, lease terms, and location context are difficult to verify. Hosts manage listings, inquiries, viewings, tenants, and payments across disconnected tools.

Product vision

Roomie is the trusted rental layer for Metro Manila: a structured marketplace where credible people and properties are easy to understand, compare, contact, and manage.

Product and source relationship

RoomieThe tentative product name and full-stack application specified in this PRD.
/mvproomieThe tested interaction portfolio. It supplies tenant and host workflows, UI patterns, and usability evidence.
/bahaytrustThe wider Philippines microhousing, market-intelligence, and trust context that informs product strategy.
/roomiedraftA separate exploratory marketplace implementation; it is not the PRD or the production architecture.

Primary jobs to be done

UserJobSuccessful outcome
RenterFind realistic options near daily destinations and understand who and what can be trusted.Confidently contact a verified host or request a viewing with full cost and living situation understood.
Host / managerPresent an available unit credibly and manage qualified interest without fragmented tools.Publish a complete verified listing, respond to inquiries, schedule viewings, and maintain a status trail.

Experience architecture

1Discover→2Filter→3Inspect→4Trust→5Understand place→6Contact

Scope boundary

P0Trust and contact

Identity/listing verification, complete facts, reviews, score explanation, chat, viewings, and reporting.

P1Decision quality

Sort, commute, transit, neighborhood context, saved search, notifications, and listing quality meter.

P2After trust

Documents, payments, receipts, escrow pilot, roommate matching, and services.

SECTION 05

From listing inspection to confident contact

The implemented listing-detail pattern is strong visually; the next MVP must add the information and trust evidence that users requested.

Required listing expansion

OccupancyCapacity, current occupants, available slots, private/shared room, roommate count, guest/pet/smoking rules.
True costBase rent, association dues, utilities, recurring fees, deposits, advance rent, and estimated move-in total.
LeaseDuration, renewal, termination, required documents, payment schedule, house rules, and contract availability.
PropertyBuilding name/age, floor, size, rooms, furnishing, accessibility, security, power/water reliability.
LocationCommute destinations, transit, daily needs, traffic/flood notes, and source timestamps.
TrustHost role, evidence checked, verification date, photo freshness, reviews, and score components.
Conversion rule. Show recurring monthly cost and estimated move-in cost before the primary contact/viewing action.

Core tenant requirements

IDCapabilityAcceptance requirement
DS-01Search and filterBudget, type, furnishing, Wi-Fi, occupancy, availability, lease length, verified-only, and commute threshold.
DS-02SortPrice, relevance, newest, commute, and trust evidence; relevance explained at a high level.
DS-03Map/list syncSelected pin and card remain synchronized; search, filters, scroll, and map position persist.
CM-01Listing-linked chatEvery thread retains listing snapshot, price/status, and a return-to-listing action.
CM-02Viewing requestRenter proposes times; host confirms or reschedules; both see status, reminders, and history.

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSTRUST AND LISTING QUALITY
SECTION 07

Trust, verification, and safety

Signals must be specific, current, explainable, and contestable. A badge is a statement about evidence checked - not a guarantee.

IDCapabilityAcceptance requirement
TR-01Identity verificationPrefer GCash Single Sign-on/KYC identity assertions if Roomie is approved as a partner; provide an equivalent manual/provider fallback. Show verification source and date, never raw credentials or documents.
TR-02Host authorityDistinguish owner, authorized representative, broker, and property manager; state the role and evidence status.
TR-03Listing verificationRecord property/address evidence, review status, reviewer type, and last verified date.
TR-04Photo integrityRequire recent coverage of the current unit; flag duplicates, generated imagery, or material edits for review.
TR-05Roomie ScoreShow components, ranges, freshness, missing evidence, and improvement steps; never present as a safety guarantee.
TR-06ReviewsLimit reviews to eligible interactions; separate host, tenant, and listing feedback; provide dispute process.
TR-07ReportingAccept reports from listings, profiles, and chat; confirm receipt, assign severity, preserve evidence, and show status.
TR-08ModerationSupport pause, removal, warning, verification hold, restrictions, audit history, and appeal.

Roomie Score safeguards

  • Use only product-relevant evidence: verification, listing completeness/freshness, response reliability, and verified-interaction history.
  • Do not use protected traits, socioeconomic proxies, unverified social media, or inferred criminality.
  • Do not convert missing evidence into a low-trust label; offer alternative verification paths.
  • Log changes and expose a plain-language explanation, correction route, and appeal.

GCash verification boundary

External dependency. GCash identity integration requires partner approval, technical onboarding, and production credentials. Roomie must never request or store a user's GCash MPIN, OTP, wallet balance, or transaction history. Until approval is secured, use a consent-based manual or accredited identity-provider fallback and label the verification source accurately.

Listing publication gate

Identity+Authority+Required facts+True cost+Current media+Availability= PUBLISHABLE

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSMETRICS AND VALIDATION
SECTION 08

Success metrics and research gates

Measure whether the deployable product produces informed, safe marketplace progress—not traffic or screen engagement alone.

North-star metric: verified qualified contact rate - eligible listing views that lead to a message or viewing request after required cost, occupancy, location, and trust information is seen.
DimensionMeasures
TrustVerification completion; badge and score comprehension; confidence to contact; report rate; substantiated misleading-listing rate.
Listing qualityRequired-field completeness; photo freshness; price/fee accuracy; stale availability; publish rejection reasons.
DiscoverySearch-to-detail; useful-result rate; filter/sort use; zero results; saves; map/list interaction.
ConversionQualified contact; viewing request; host response; scheduled viewing; cancellation/no-show; response time.
SafetyReports per interaction; urgent response; resolution time; appeal overturns; repeat offenders; blocked contacts.

Product acceptance gates

GateMinimum evidence
Renter journeySearch → listing → message/viewing completes on desktop and mobile with persisted state and no critical error.
Host journeyCreate → submit → verify → publish → inquiry/viewing management completes with role enforcement.
Decision informationMonthly cost, move-in cost, occupancy, lease, availability, location, and verification source are visible before contact.
Safety operationsReports, evidence, moderation action, appeal, and audit events are usable end-to-end by authorized operators.
Production readinessAutomated tests, security checks, migrations, backups, monitoring, runbook, and rollback pass in staging.

Instrumentation required at launch

Track search, listing impressions/details, trust-detail views, saves, messages, viewing state changes, host response time, listing completeness, reports, moderation outcomes, and errors. Do not send raw identity evidence, message contents, or sensitive personal data to analytics.

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSENGINEERING SPECIFICATION
SECTION 09

Full-stack implementation boundary

The first production pilot is a responsive web application backed by persistent services. The architecture may evolve, but these capabilities and controls are required.

Logical architecture

LayerRequired responsibility
ClientResponsive renter and host web experiences, accessible navigation, resilient form states, and explicit loading/error/empty states.
Application/APIAuthentication, roles, profiles, listings, matching/search, inquiries, chat, viewings, verification, reporting, moderation, and notifications.
DataRelational system of record, private object storage for media/evidence, geospatial search, immutable audit events, retention/deletion controls, and backups.
IntegrationsGCash identity if approved; email/SMS or push; maps/geocoding. Payments remain out of the first production pilot.
OperationsAdmin review queues, feature flags, analytics consent, monitoring, incident response, rate limits, and environment separation.

Platform requirements

IDCapabilityAcceptance requirement
PL-01Accounts and rolesSupport renter, host/manager, moderator, and administrator permissions with server-enforced authorization and account recovery.
PL-02Listings and mediaPersist drafts, versions, verification state, availability, structured costs, occupancy, and optimized media with private evidence storage.
PL-03Search and matchingIndex approved listings by location and required filters; exclude paused, expired, rejected, or unavailable inventory.
PL-04CommunicationPersist listing-linked conversations and viewing state; prevent unauthorized thread access; support notification preferences.
PL-05Trust operationsRecord evidence metadata, reviewer decisions, reports, actions, appeals, and actor/timestamp audit trails.
PL-06Reliability and privacyEncrypt in transit/at rest, minimize personal data, log safely, back up data, rate-limit abuse, and document recovery and deletion procedures.

CTO decisions required before build

D1Architecture

Framework, API boundary, database, geospatial search, media pipeline, hosting, environments, and deployment ownership.

D2Identity and privacy

Authentication provider, GCash feasibility, fallback KYC, consent, retention, access control, and incident response.

D3Marketplace operations

Verification SLAs, moderation queue, support escalation, notification channels, analytics events, and pilot geography.

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSAI BUILD CONTRACT
SECTION 10

Implementation contract for coding agents

Use this contract with the functional requirements in Sections 05–09. An implementation may change technologies through a documented architecture decision, but it may not silently change product scope or acceptance behavior.

Reference stack

ConcernDefault implementation
ApplicationTypeScript; Next.js responsive web client and server/API routes; shared runtime validation and typed contracts.
DataPostgreSQL with PostGIS; versioned migrations; transactional writes; seed data separated from production data.
IdentityManaged authentication with email/phone recovery; server-side RBAC for renter, host/manager, moderator, and admin.
Files/jobsS3-compatible private object storage, signed URLs, image processing, and a durable background-job mechanism.
QualityUnit/integration tests plus Playwright critical-journey tests; structured logs, error tracking, health checks, and analytics consent.

Canonical domain model

Entity groupRequired records and relationships
IdentityUser, Role, Profile, Consent, VerificationCase, VerificationEvidence metadata. Evidence objects remain private.
InventoryProperty, Listing, ListingVersion, Unit, CostItem, Amenity, Availability, Media, HostAuthority, Location.
MarketplaceSavedListing, Conversation, ConversationParticipant, Message, ViewingRequest, NotificationPreference.
Trust operationsReview, Report, ModerationCase, ModerationAction, Appeal, RoomieScoreSnapshot, AuditEvent.

Required state machines

Listingdraft → submitted → under_review → published → paused | rented | expired; under_review → needs_changes | rejected.
Verificationunverified → pending → verified | needs_action | rejected | expired.
Viewingproposed → confirmed | rescheduled → completed | cancelled | no_show.
Reportopen → triaged → investigating → actioned | dismissed → appealed → closed.
Agent constraint. Never simulate a production integration. GCash, maps, messaging, and email/SMS must use provider adapters, environment-based credentials, explicit sandbox/mock modes, and safe failure states.

ROOMIE MANILA - PRODUCT REQUIREMENTSDEPLOYMENT ACCEPTANCE
SECTION 11

Deployable deliverable

“Complete” means a running, testable system with operational controls—not generated screens or a local demo.

Required application surfaces

IDSurfaceRequired result
DL-01Public/renterSearch, filters, map/list, listing detail, trust explanation, save, message, viewing request, report, account settings.
DL-02HostOnboarding, authority/identity submission, listing editor/preview, publish status, inquiries, chat, viewings, notifications.
DL-03OperationsVerification and report queues, evidence review, actions/appeals, user/listing history, audit lookup, least-privilege access.
DL-04PlatformAuthentication, persistence, media storage, geospatial search, notifications, background jobs, audit events, observability.

Interface contract

ResourceMinimum operations
/api/listingsSearch/read; host create/update/submit/pause; operator approve/request-changes/reject. Enforce visibility by state and role.
/api/conversationsCreate from listing, list authorized threads, send/read messages, block/report. Preserve listing snapshot.
/api/viewingsPropose, confirm, reschedule, cancel, complete/no-show with actor, timestamp, and notifications.
/api/verificationsCreate case, attach private evidence metadata, provider callback, manual review, expire/revoke; never expose secrets.
/api/reportsSubmit, triage, action, appeal, close; write immutable audit events for every privileged change.

Definition of done

  • Production, staging, and preview environments deploy from version control with documented configuration and no committed secrets.
  • Database migrations, rollback procedure, backups/restore test, seed/demo accounts, API documentation, and an operator runbook are included.
  • Critical renter, host, and operator journeys pass automated tests; authorization, file access, validation, rate limits, and common abuse cases are tested.
  • Responsive accessibility, loading/empty/error states, monitoring alerts, dependency/license review, and privacy/retention behavior pass release review.
  • A handoff README explains local setup, architecture, environment variables, deployment, test commands, known limitations, and next decisions.
Release rule: if a required external provider is unavailable, ship a clearly labeled sandbox adapter or defer the feature. Do not present mock verification or notifications as real.

SECTION 12

Delivery plan and ownership

Build one complete vertical slice, prove it in staging, then expand. Do not generate the entire surface area before identity, permissions, persistence, and moderation work end-to-end.

StageTimeOutcomeOwners
0. DecideWeek 1Approve architecture, schema, providers, environments, trust policy, pilot geography, acceptance tests, and ADRs.CTO, Product, Design, Trust/Safety
1. FoundationWeeks 2–3Repo, CI/CD, environments, auth/RBAC, database/migrations, storage, observability, seed data, design tokens.Engineering
2. Vertical sliceWeeks 4–6Host draft/submission → operator approval → renter search/detail → message/viewing, fully persisted and tested.Engineering, Product, Design
3. HardenWeeks 7–8Reporting/moderation, notifications, failure states, accessibility, security/privacy review, load checks, backup/restore.Engineering, Trust/Safety
4. PilotAfter gatesLimited verified inventory, monitored production release, support coverage, incident/rollback readiness, metrics review.Product, CTO, Operations

Highest risks

RiskSeverityPrimary mitigation
False assurance from badges or scoreHighSpecific labels, evidence/date disclosure, no guarantees, comprehension tests, appeal.
Discrimination through profiles/rankingHighPermitted-field policy, protected-trait review, fairness tests, enforcement, recourse.
Fraud adapts to verificationHighLayered checks, freshness, anomaly review, reports, holds, human escalation.
Thin verified inventoryHighFocused geography, assisted onboarding, quality support, active freshness operations.
Prototype mistaken for productionMediumExplicit boundary, architecture/security review, persistence and failure testing.
Payment and regulatory exposureHighDefer processing; assess licensed partners and obligations before build.

APPENDIX A

Evidence-to-decision traceability

Every major change is connected to user research or an implemented prototype pattern.

DecisionEvidenceImplemented reference
Trust infrastructure is P0.Testing made trust, accurate information, and transparent cost the primary build focus.Verified-host treatment and Roomie Score concepts in tenant detail/profile screens.
MVP2 is the discovery baseline.MVP2 produced the strongest tenant-testing outcome.Split map/list sheet, listing cards, map sync, and viewing request in /mvp2/.
Curated rails remain secondary.Users value local discovery, but core decision information remains primary.Neighborhood/budget rails in /mvp3/.
Host operations precede live payments.Hosts valued payments, but research recommends trust and communication first.Dashboard, listings, inquiries, calendar, and payment concepts across host routes.
Complete cost, occupancy, and location.Requests for roommates, capacity, fees, lease terms, availability, commute, transit, flood/traffic, and daily needs.Extend existing listing-detail and map structures rather than replacing them.
GCash is a conditional identity path.GCash offers partner identity solutions, but access requires approval and onboarding.Integrate only through approved partner APIs; retain an equivalent fallback and never collect MPIN or OTP.
The pilot requires a real backend.The tested prototypes use mock state and do not validate persistence, permissions, moderation, or failure recovery.Platform requirements PL-01 to PL-06 define the production boundary.
